summary: An excerpt from a fiction book (labeled 'Book 15 — part 78') in which Ray and Emma flirt intimately at close quarters. Ray, feeling scared by his attraction to her, is unsettled when Emma says he has been lonely for a long time. His reflections turn to his past as a military leader who had his soldiers seek release before battle, and he worries that loneliness leads to poor judgment. The passage ends with Emma noticing he has drifted off mentally, and Ray admitting he has never said anything like that to a woman.
one_line: Ray and Emma flirt intimately, but Ray grows troubled by Emma's remark that he is lonely and recalls his wartime practices.
key_facts: Ray tells Emma that she is the most beautiful thing he has ever seen, and says that his feeling this way scares him.
Emma tells Ray that he has been lonely for a very long time.
Ray thinks loneliness is a step away from desperation and that lonely men make stupid mistakes.
Ray recalls that before a major tactical engagement he made his men go into the nearest town and seek sexual release.
Ray says that if a soldier lacked money for such release, Ray gave it to him.
Ray believes the soldiers who returned were brighter-eyed, firmer in step, and less prone to trembling hands, though still scared.
Ray says of the soldiers that getting laid was not going to save their lives on the battlefield but gave them a perspective that kept them from making fatal mistakes.
Ray tells Emma that he is not lonely, and Emma replies that he is lonely for her and lonely and hungry.
Emma says the playful flirtation has turned to questioning, bordering on concern, because Ray has drifted into his own thoughts.
Ray admits to Emma that he has never said anything like that to a woman.
Emma responds to Ray's admission with delight, asking whether it was never.

entities.name: Ray
entities.role: Male protagonist who flirts with Emma, reflects on his loneliness, and recalls having led soldiers before battle

entities.name: Emma
entities.role: Female character who flirts with Ray and suggests he has been lonely
